blogs.title: From Tokens to Sequences: Why AI Training Was Breaking Down—And How a Simple Shift Fixed It
blogs.description: This post breaks down the core insight behind GSPO: that the popular GRPO algorithm was applying importance sampling at the wrong level—token by token—introducing high-variance noise that accumulated over long responses and caused catastrophic model collapse. We explain in plain terms why the unit of optimization should match the unit of reward, and how GSPO's shift to sequence-level importance ratios and clipping aligns with this principle, resulting in dramatically more stable and efficient RL training for large language models.

blogs.title: Taming the Experts: How GSPO Solved Mixture-of-Experts Training Instability Without Band-Aids
blogs.description: This post explores a major practical win of GSPO: its ability to stabilize RL training for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models. We walk readers through the 'expert-activation volatility' problem—where the experts activated for a given response keep changing after each gradient update, wrecking token-level importance ratios—and explain how the previous workaround (Routing Replay) added overhead and limited model capacity. We then show how GSPO's sequence-level focus sidesteps this issue entirely, eliminating the need for complex stabilization strategies.

blogs.title: More Clipping, Better Results: The Counterintuitive Secret Behind GSPO's Training Efficiency
blogs.description: This post dives into one of the paper's most surprising findings: GSPO clips roughly two orders of magnitude more tokens than GRPO, yet still achieves higher training efficiency and better benchmark performance. We unpack why this counterintuitive result makes sense—GRPO's token-level gradient estimates are inherently noisy, so clipping more of them is actually a feature, not a bug—and what this tells us about the quality of learning signals in RL for language models.

blogs.title: Inside Qwen3: How a New Reinforcement Learning Algorithm Unlocked the Next Leap in AI Reasoning
blogs.description: This post tells the story of GSPO's real-world impact: its successful application to the RL training of the latest Qwen3 models. We cover the journey from identifying GRPO's instability as a bottleneck to scaling RL with GSPO, the empirical results on benchmarks like AIME'24, LiveCodeBench, and CodeForces, and what this means for the future of scaling reinforcement learning with language models. The post frames GSPO as a scalable algorithmic cornerstone that could enable continued capability advances.

blogs.title: Less Infrastructure, More Intelligence: How GSPO Could Simplify the AI Training Pipeline
blogs.description: This post focuses on GSPO's potential to streamline RL infrastructure—a topic often overlooked but crucial for practitioners. Because GSPO operates on sequence-level likelihoods, which are more tolerant of numerical precision discrepancies, it may eliminate the need to recompute old-policy likelihoods with the training engine, allowing direct use of likelihoods from inference engines like vLLM and SGLang. We discuss the implications for partial rollout, multi-turn RL, and training-inference disaggregated frameworks, painting a picture of leaner, simpler RL pipelines.
